result.title: ParaBlock++: Communication-Computation Parallel Blockwise Hierarchical Federated Learning
result.comment: A journal version extended from the published conference version
result.summary: In the emerging 6G paradigm, where AI-driven services operate over decentralized and resource-constrained infrastructures, the convergence of distributed learning algorithms remains a significant challenge. This paper introduces $\mathrm{ParaBlock}$++, a low Earth orbit (LEO) satellite-assisted hierarchical federated learning (HFL) framework, enabling resource-limited terrestrial clients to collaboratively engage in federated learning (FL) via ground-satellite links (GSLs) supported by LEO satellite megaconstellations. Within this architecture, LEO satellites serve multiple roles: as edge servers aggregating and broadcasting models, as clients accelerating training, and as high-throughput relays managing inter-satellite routing through inter-satellite links (ISLs). Departing from conventional synchronous Jacobian-type updates, $\mathrm{ParaBlock}$++ employs asynchronous BCD-type updates to enhance convergence speed. We provide theoretical convergence guarantees for convex, strongly convex, and non-convex objectives, and formulate optimization problems to determine optimal cluster resource allocation and model partitioning for minimizing global training latency. Experimental evaluations demonstrate that $\mathrm{ParaBlock}$++ achieves faster initial convergence and comparable final performance for deep neural networks (DNNs) such as ResNet-18, offering promising directions for federated learning across geographically remote areas enabled by 6G technologies, but much less global rounds and communication cost.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 ParaBlock++，一种 LEO 卫星辅助的分层联邦学习框架，用异步分块（BCD 型）更新替代同步更新，并给出收敛性分析与时延优化，在 ResNet-18 等 DNN 上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 工作属于分布式训练系统与通信调度，异步分块更新只是系统层面的收敛加速手段，缺乏与视觉证据、latent 推理状态生成或停止决策的具体机制线索，因此不纳入。
